answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 17% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the copper balance is debited each close, the terrace ledger shows the bleed, and the dawn audit lists every fee. An operator holding 91 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
